questions.q: What does the summary mean by metathinking?
a: Thinking about your own thinking
Thinking faster than you usually do
Thinking without using any words
Thinking about other people's motives
questions.why: Lesson 1 defines metathinking as thinking about thinking, which lets you observe your own mind.

questions.q: Why does the summary say you can log into your mind as a superuser?
a: Because you are separate from your brain and can observe it
Because your brain stores an unlimited amount of information
Because old habits can be erased in a single day
Because emotions never affect clear thinking
questions.why: Lesson 1 says we are separate from our brains, which is why we can notice ourselves thinking.

questions.q: What are the two kinds of attention described in the summary?
a: Voluntary and reflexive
Focused and creative
Passive and active
Internal and external
questions.why: Lesson 2 distinguishes deliberately directing focus from reacting to an outside stimulus.

questions.q: Why does an unchecked notification create anxiety, according to the summary?
a: The mind feels it has unfinished business
The phone uses more battery in the background
You fear missing an urgent work message
The sound keeps interrupting your breathing
questions.why: Lesson 2 says the brain believes something is left to finish, which stresses it.

questions.q: What is the purpose of imagining your own funeral in the summary's exercises?
a: It shows how you want to treat people now
It helps you plan your finances for later
It reveals which career suits you best
It measures how many friends you have
questions.why: Lesson 3 says the way you hope to be remembered is how you should behave with others.
